982c3ec0ec53e7a7.title: Critical Integer‑Overflow in VMware Workstation/Fusion Enables Host Code Execution
982c3ec0ec53e7a7.summary: Broadcom patched CVE‑2026‑59346, a critical integer‑overflow in VMware Workstation and Fusion (versions 25H2/26H1) that lets a locally‑privileged VM user execute arbitrary code on the host via the VMXNET3 adapter. The flaw scores 9.3 CVSS and has no work‑around.
982c3ec0ec53e7a7.impact: Attackers who gain administrative rights inside a VM can break out to the hypervisor, compromising the entire host and any other VMs running on it.
982c3ec0ec53e7a7.action: Apply the VMware Workstation 26H1u1 and VMware Fusion 26H1u1 updates immediately.

0c97dcbaac2a5941.title: JetBrains Cadence Compromised via Critical TeamCity Vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑63077)
0c97dcbaac2a5941.summary: Unpatched TeamCity allowed threat actors to exploit CVE‑2026‑63077, a deserialization flaw with a CVSS 9.8 score, to breach JetBrains Cadence. Attackers accessed the Cadence server, extracted AWS credentials, and copied backup data from 2024, potentially exposing current user workloads and secrets.
0c97dcbaac2a5941.impact: Security teams must treat all Cadence executions, inputs, outputs, and stored credentials as compromised, and recognize the broader risk of unpatched CI/CD tools in supply‑chain attacks.
0c97dcbaac2a5941.action: Immediately revoke or rotate all AWS and other credentials stored in Cadence and audit all Cadence workloads for malicious activity.

88d106f1bb825bd4.title: Linux kernel maintainer releases multiple stable updates fixing bugs and security issues
88d106f1bb825bd4.summary: Greg Kroah‑Hartman published eight new stable Linux kernels on September 2 (7.2.3, 7.1.13, 6.18.49, 6.12.108, 6.6.156, 6.1.187, 5.15.220, 5.10.269) and three additional releases on September 7 (7.2.4, 6.18.50, 6.12.109). Each release bundles extensive bug fixes and security patches across the tree, and 7.1.13 marks the final update for the 7.1 series.
88d106f1bb825bd4.impact: The updates close numerous vulnerabilities and stability regressions, reducing attack surface for systems running the listed kernel versions.
88d106f1bb825bd4.action: Upgrade all Linux hosts to the newest stable kernel for their series immediately.

3699d96dcf48c22c.title: Multiple Linux Distributions Release Broad Security Updates Across Core Packages
3699d96dcf48c22c.summary: All major Linux distributions released a wave of security patches this week, covering critical components such as dbus-broker, freerdp, nodejs, php, openssl, kernel, and graphics libraries. The updates span AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Oracle Linux, and Mageia, addressing numerous vulnerabilities without referencing specific CVE identifiers.
3699d96dcf48c22c.impact: Unpatched systems remain exposed to potential remote code execution, privilege escalation, and denial‑of‑service attacks in the affected packages. The breadth of the updates means that many production environments may be vulnerable if the patches are not applied promptly.
3699d96dcf48c22c.action: Apply the latest security updates from your distribution’s package manager without delay.

dd5a568c6d3e40c6.title: Grml 2026.09 Live Distribution Released with Linux 7.1.8 Kernel and exFAT Boot Support
dd5a568c6d3e40c6.summary: Grml 2026.09, codenamed “Hättiwaritätti,” ships as a Debian‑based live distro for sysadmins, built on upcoming Debian 14 (forky). It upgrades to the Linux 7.1.8 kernel, adds native exFAT boot capability, and bundles GNU Screen 5.0.1, delivering newer hardware support without new security advisories.
dd5a568c6d3e40c6.impact: The kernel upgrade brings broader hardware compatibility and performance improvements, but introduces no immediate security patches or CVEs to address. Existing Grml deployments remain secure, but administrators should verify compatibility with their hardware and tooling.
dd5a568c6d3e40c6.action: Upgrade to Grml 2026.09 after testing boot on exFAT media and confirming kernel compatibility with critical workloads.

21263e7ebe9581a1.title: FBI Launches Investigation into Dark‑Web Service Selling 153 Million North American Driver’s Licenses
21263e7ebe9581a1.summary: A new dark‑web marketplace, Nexus, is offering digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian driver’s licenses, along with millions of other ID documents, sourced from a widely used identity‑verification provider in Louisiana. The FBI’s New Orleans field office has opened a formal probe into the data breach.
21263e7ebe9581a1.impact: Security teams must assume that personal identification data of millions of users has been compromised, increasing the risk of identity theft, fraud, and credential stuffing attacks. Any systems that ingest or validate driver’s license images from the implicated provider are now exposed to potential abuse.
21263e7ebe9581a1.action: Immediately audit and, if necessary, replace any third‑party identity‑verification services that source driver’s license images from the Louisiana provider, and monitor for suspicious activity involving compromised IDs.

cc32169d9af5f5da.title: Unicode‑Tag “ASCII Smuggling” Powers Massive Finance‑Themed Phishing Campaign
cc32169d9af5f5da.summary: Microsoft detected a high‑volume phishing operation that injects invisible Unicode tag characters (U+E0000‑U+E007F) into finance‑related keywords, splitting words like “funding” to bypass Office 365 email filters. The campaign peaked at 2.5 million messages per day in February, then fell sharply after mid‑May, but remains active.
cc32169d9af5f5da.impact: Security teams see traditional keyword‑based filters rendered ineffective against this Unicode‑based obfuscation, while Defender for Office 365 still blocks >99 % of the mail using other signals.
cc32169d9af5f5da.action: Update email security policies to include detection of Unicode tag characters and enable Microsoft Defender for Office 365’s Unicode‑smuggling signatures.

c95e648fd687a543.title: PostgreSQL Patches 12‑Year‑Old Logical Decoding Vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑6471)
c95e648fd687a543.summary: PostgreSQL released updates fixing CVE‑2026‑6471, a critical 7.2‑rated flaw that lets any REPLICATION‑enabled account execute arbitrary OS‑level code via logical decoding output plugins. The bug, present since logical decoding debuted in version 9.4 (2014), is mitigated by a new whitelist parameter restricting loadable plugin libraries.
c95e648fd687a543.impact: Attackers can compromise database hosts by abusing replication users in CDC, backup, or standby setups, potentially gaining full system control.
c95e648fd687a543.action: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, or 14.24 (or later) and verify the output_plugin_libraries whitelist is configured.

018c9450de11b26e.title: Ted Backdoor Embedded in Compromised HAProxy Binaries Enables Stealth Web Traffic Interception
018c9450de11b26e.summary: A custom Linux toolkit named Ted was compiled into trojanized HAProxy load balancers at two South Korean firms, allowing attackers to hijack HTTP requests, serve forged pages, and exfiltrate data via hidden C2 channels that bypass backend logs and HAProxy statistics.
018c9450de11b26e.impact: Security teams must treat HAProxy binaries as potential infection vectors, as the implant can silently intercept and modify traffic while evading traditional monitoring.
018c9450de11b26e.action: Audit all HAProxy binaries for unauthorized modifications, verify code signatures, and redeploy from trusted sources while tightening host execution controls.

d4908d4411cee4ef.title: Over 440,000 Exploit Attempts Target Critical WordPress Super Forms and Elementor Pro RCE Flaws
d4908d4411cee4ef.summary: Threat actors have launched more than 440,000 exploit attempts against two critical WordPress plugin vulnerabilities—CVE-2026-14894 in Super Forms and CVE-2026-32475 in Elementor Pro—allowing unauthenticated file uploads that lead to remote code execution.
d4908d4411cee4ef.impact: These attacks can drop PHP web shells, create admin accounts, exfiltrate data, and fully compromise WordPress sites using the vulnerable plugins.
d4908d4411cee4ef.action: Update Super Forms to 6.3.314 and Elementor Pro to 4.2.2 immediately, and block malicious POST requests to admin-ajax.php.

f681859afb2558e2.title: Plex Issues Critical Patch for Multiple Undisclosed Vulnerabilities in Media Server 1.43.3 and Desktop 1.115.0
f681859afb2558e2.summary: Plex released updates for Media Server 1.43.3 and Desktop 1.115.0 that fix several security flaws, prompting an immediate upgrade recommendation. While the specific issues remain undisclosed, Plex has requested CVE identifiers and references a prior high‑severity bug (CVE‑2025‑34158) that exposed admin tokens via the /myplex/account endpoint.
f681859afb2558e2.impact: Unpatched Plex instances remain vulnerable to potential unauthorized access and infrastructure discovery, increasing the attack surface for media environments, especially on exposed NAS deployments.
f681859afb2558e2.action: Upgrade all Plex Media Server and Desktop installations to the latest versions without delay, and manually install the packages on NAS devices if the package manager lacks the update.

b3af9547e5b871ac.title: Google Patches Actively Exploited Chrome V8 Zero‑Day (CVE‑2026‑85046)
b3af9547e5b871ac.summary: Google released Chrome 152.0.7977.82/.83 for Windows and macOS and 152.0.7977.82 for Linux, fixing a type‑confusion vulnerability in the V8 engine (CVE‑2026‑85046, CVSS 8.8) that is confirmed to be exploited in the wild. The update also addresses 11 additional high‑severity bugs across Chrome components.
b3af9547e5b871ac.impact: The flaw allowed remote code execution within Chrome’s sandbox via a crafted HTML page, putting browsers and any downstream Chromium‑based products at immediate risk of compromise. Security teams must assume active exploitation across the enterprise.
b3af9547e5b871ac.action: Deploy the Chrome 152.0.7977.82/.83 update immediately on all Windows, macOS, and Linux endpoints and ensure downstream Chromium browsers are patched as soon as vendors release the fix.
affected_systems: Chromium‑based browsers (Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) when updates are released

cc5cc22ecd29e6b7.title: OpenAI Unveils GPT‑6 Astra, Achieves Perfect 100% Score on ExploitBench
cc5cc22ecd29e6b7.summary: OpenAI launched GPT‑6 Astra, branding it the world’s most intelligent and aligned model. Astra hit a flawless 100% on ExploitBench, surpassing GPT‑5.6 Sol’s 78.5% and demonstrating the ability to generate working exploits from recent vulnerabilities, including two zero‑days disclosed between June and August 2026. The model is initially limited to secure code‑review use cases.
cc5cc22ecd29e6b7.impact: Security teams must recognize that Astra can automate exploit creation at unprecedented accuracy, raising the risk of rapid weaponization of newly disclosed flaws.
cc5cc22ecd29e6b7.action: Begin monitoring OpenAI’s API usage policies and integrate AI‑assisted code‑review tools while tightening exploit detection and response processes.

c1ee648924c4fd9c.title: Microsoft Teams Abuse Enables Human‑Operated Intrusions and Remote‑Control Malware Deployments
c1ee648924c4fd9c.summary: Microsoft reports a human‑operated intrusion campaign that exploits external Microsoft Teams collaboration to impersonate IT staff, trick users into granting remote sessions, and then deploys PowerShell‑downloaded MSI payloads that install a Node.js runtime and obfuscated JavaScript implant for persistent C2 and AD reconnaissance.
c1ee648924c4fd9c.impact: Security teams face direct interactive access by attackers who can move laterally via WinRM to high‑value assets such as domain controllers, bypassing traditional perimeter defenses.
c1ee648924c4fd9c.action: Implement strict verification for all Teams external‑collaboration invites, enforce MFA for remote session approvals, and block unauthorized MSI installations via application control policies.

e2b22f2043a179f6.title: Critical Cisco Nexus 9000 Vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑20212) Allows Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution as Root
e2b22f2043a179f6.summary: Cisco patched a critical flaw in ten Silicon One‑based Nexus 9000 switches (CVE‑2026‑20212, CVSS 9.8) that exposes TCP ports 43210/43211 in the default VRF, enabling unauthenticated attackers to inject crafted payloads that execute with root privileges or crash the S1HAL process. No known exploits exist, but the risk is severe.
e2b22f2043a179f6.impact: Security teams must treat any reachable Nexus 9000 device as compromised until mitigations are applied, as attackers can gain full control without credentials.
e2b22f2043a179f6.action: Apply Cisco’s released patches immediately and block ports 43210/43211 with an infrastructure ACL or Live Protect shield as a temporary control.

65c657640f556fe0.title: BraZetsu Malware Turns Compromised Windows Hosts Into Marketplace Inventory
65c657640f556fe0.summary: Researchers detail BraZetsu, a Python‑based Windows malware framework that enables Initial Access Brokers to monetize compromised systems via an underground marketplace, leveraging AI‑driven reconnaissance, CNAB financial file theft, and browser‑history extraction.
65c657640f556fe0.impact: Security teams face a new supply‑chain style threat that converts any infected Windows endpoint into a sellable asset, expanding the attack surface and increasing the urgency of detection and containment.
65c657640f556fe0.action: Deploy behavior‑based detection for BraZetsu’s modular components, block its C2 domains, and audit Windows hosts for unauthorized data exfiltration of financial and browsing records.

dcb783b33acb3d05.title: Thomson Reuters' West Publishing C‑Track Court Management Platform Breached, Exposing SSNs and Sealed Data
dcb783b33acb3d05.summary: An unauthorized party accessed files from West Publishing's C‑Track court case management system in March 2026, compromising records from courts in 11 U.S. states, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Ontario, Canada. Exposed data includes names, Social Security numbers, driver’s license numbers, dates of birth, medical and health‑insurance information, and some sealed documents.
dcb783b33acb3d05.impact: Security teams must assume that personally identifiable information (PII) from thousands of court filings is now searchable by threat actors, increasing the risk of identity theft and targeted fraud against affected individuals and legal professionals.
dcb783b33acb3d05.action: Immediately review any integration with C‑Track, audit access logs for suspicious activity, and notify affected users while enrolling them in the offered credit‑monitoring services.
affected_systems: West Publishing C‑Track court case management platform

0d90c8a062a562db.title: US Leads Global RMM Phishing Campaign Targeting 46 Countries
0d90c8a062a562db.summary: A remote‑monitoring‑and‑management (RMM) phishing operation has hit 46 nations, with 45% of activity focused on the United States. Attackers distribute fake tax forms, shipping notices and other documents to trick victims into installing legitimate RMM tools, using rapidly rotated Vercel, GitHub Pages, Netlify and cloud storage infrastructure.
0d90c8a062a562db.impact: Security teams must assume that any seemingly legitimate RMM installation could be malicious, and traditional IOC‑based detection will miss the fast‑changing delivery hosts.
0d90c8a062a562db.action: Deploy behavior‑based monitoring for RMM tool execution and block unauthorized remote‑admin connections.

b79f1fe02f7b383b.title: Threat Actors Abuse Legitimate Node.js Runtime to Deploy Malware in Targeted Campaigns
b79f1fe02f7b383b.summary: Since February 2026, attackers have been downloading the official Node.js installer and using the signed node.exe binary to execute malicious JavaScript, chain PowerShell commands, and install back‑doors such as ModeloRAT, Mistic, and GateKeeper on government, technology and hospitality targets.
b79f1fe02f7b383b.impact: Security teams face increased risk of evading signature‑based detection because the payload runs inside a trusted developer tool and persists via a Registry Run key.
b79f1fe02f7b383b.action: Deploy application whitelisting, monitor for unexpected node.exe executions, and enforce strict code‑signing verification for Node.js binaries.

a6874e4cf62c00d4.title: Shai‑Hulud Worm Expands Credential Harvesting to 469 Locations Across DevOps and Cloud Environments
a6874e4cf62c00d4.summary: GitGuardian discovered that the latest Shai‑Hulud infostealer variant now scans 469 credential stores—including developer workstations, CI/CD pipelines, cloud configs, and AI tool settings—doubling the coverage of earlier versions and enabling attackers to hijack trusted supply‑chain relationships.
a6874e4cf62c00d4.impact: Security teams must treat credential leakage as the primary attack vector, as compromised tokens can cascade from source code to cloud infrastructure and package registries.
a6874e4cf62c00d4.action: Audit and rotate all secrets, enforce least‑privilege policies, and implement secret‑detection tooling across the entire development lifecycle.

a43d39f57668b259.title: Pegasus Zero‑Click iMessage Exploit Compromises Serbian Student Activist’s iPhone
a43d39f57668b259.summary: Citizen Lab and the SHARE Foundation confirmed that a zero‑click iMessage exploit was used to install NSO Group’s Pegasus spyware on the iPhone of a Serbian student protest movement member, with infection dates spanning December 2025 to January 2026. Apple patched the flaw in iOS 18.4.1 (April 2025).
a43d39f57668b259.impact: Security teams must assume that any iOS device that received iMessage traffic before the iOS 18.4.1 patch could be silently compromised, exposing calls, messages, location, and credentials. The attack demonstrates that state‑level spyware can bypass user interaction entirely.
a43d39f57668b259.action: Deploy Apple’s iOS 18.4.1 or later to all iPhones, enforce mobile device management checks for Pegasus indicators, and notify potentially affected users to review Apple’s threat‑notification alerts.

aaff398b652d04e4.title: CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor Privilege‑Escalation Zero‑Day ‘FalconFlank’ Enables SYSTEM Access
aaff398b652d04e4.summary: Researcher Nightmare Eclipse released a zero‑day exploit, FalconFlank, that abuses CrowdStrike Falcon’s Office malicious‑macros remediation to spawn a SYSTEM‑level command prompt on fully patched Windows 11 25H2 and Windows Server 2025 hosts.
aaff398b652d04e4.impact: The flaw gives attackers immediate SYSTEM privileges on any endpoint running the latest CrowdStrike Falcon sensor, bypassing existing protections and enabling full control of the host.
aaff398b652d04e4.action: Disable the Microsoft Office File Suspicious Macro Removal policy setting in CrowdStrike and verify protection via Cloud Anti‑malware for Office files.

72546cef7609b95e.title: CISA Flags Seven Actively Exploited Flaws; SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero‑Days Enable Unauthenticated RCE
72546cef7609b95e.summary: CISA added seven vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog, including two zero‑day flaws in SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances (CVE‑2026‑83548, CVE‑2026‑83549) that attackers are chaining to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution, while other high‑severity bugs affect Sangoma Switchvox, JFrog Artifactory, Kludex Starlette, Kestra OSS, and Berri LiteLLM.
72546cef7609b95e.impact: Security teams must assume these flaws are being weaponised in the wild, with the SonicWall chain providing a direct path to full system compromise and the other bugs exposing critical infrastructure to data theft and ransomware.
72546cef7609b95e.action: Immediately apply SonicWall hotfixes 12.4.3‑03526 or 12.5.0‑02952, patch all other listed products, and scan for indicators of compromise.
affected_systems: Berri LiteLLM Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint

d25c5544f172caaa.title: Google Launches Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber and Fairwind Program for Trusted Defenders
d25c5544f172caaa.summary: Google unveiled Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, its most capable cybersecurity AI model, and opened it to high‑priority defenders through the Fairwind Program, targeting governments, healthcare, telecoms and over 650 partners including CrowdStrike, Datadog, Menlo Security, Palo Alto Networks, and Snowflake.
d25c5544f172caaa.impact: Security teams gain early access to a frontier‑level AI that excels at autonomous vulnerability discovery and fixing, giving them a measurable advantage over attackers.
d25c5544f172caaa.action: Enroll in the Fairwind Program or partner with Google Cloud to integrate Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber into your vulnerability management and threat‑hunting workflows.
